choices.title: Consolidate and make a plan
choices.body: Spreadsheet time. Real numbers. Real timeline. Real discipline.

choices.title: Take a high-paying contract to clear it
choices.body: Sell three months of your life. Buy back your financial freedom.

choices.title: Declare bankruptcy, start over
choices.body: Nuclear option. Reset everything. The shame is temporary. The relief is immediate.

title: The Sponsorship DM
body: A developer tools company DMs you: '$2,000/month to mention us in your posts.' You have 15K followers. The product is fine. Not great. The money would cover rent. Your audience trusts you. That trust is worth more than $2,000. Or is it worth exactly $2,000?

choices.title: Take the sponsorship, be transparent
choices.body: Disclose it. Be honest. Take the money. Hope they don't suck.

choices.title: Decline, protect the audience
choices.body: Your credibility isn't for sale. Not for $2,000. Maybe for more. No. Not for more.

choices.title: Counter with a higher rate
choices.body: If they want your audience, pay market rate. You're not a charity.

title: The Sabbatical Clock
body: Your sabbatical is ending. You feel better. Not fixed, but better. The world kept spinning without you optimizing it. Now the question: go back to what you were, or become something else? The answer feels obvious until you check your bank account.

choices.title: Re-enter the market, refreshed
choices.body: Go back. But differently this time. With boundaries. (You hope.)

choices.title: Extend the break, risk the runway
choices.body: You're not ready. Give yourself more time. The money will figure itself out.

choices.title: Pivot entirely, new direction
choices.body: Don't go back. Go somewhere else. Anywhere else.

title: The Industry Is Small
body: You burned a bridge. The industry is small. The person you burned now runs engineering at a company you desperately want to join. They're on the hiring committee. A mutual friend's face said everything.

choices.title: Reach out and apologize directly
choices.body: Eat humble pie. Write the email. Mean every word. Send it.

choices.title: Apply anyway, hope they forgot
choices.body: Maybe they moved on. People forget. (People do not forget.)

choices.title: Target a different company entirely
choices.body: Avoid the blast radius. Find another path. There's always another path.

title: Panic Attack at the Demo
body: Livestream. New model. It solves distributed consensus — the problem your entire discipline spent four decades on. On stage. To applause. Forty years of research. Forty seconds of compute. Your chest locks. Hands shake. Laptop closed. Floor. Forty minutes of your body remembering every system it ever built.

choices.title: Full week offline
choices.body: Everything off. No demos. No launches. Just a body in a room, remembering it's a body.

choices.title: Grief therapist, not regular therapy
choices.body: Not anxiety. Grief. For a career. For a field. For the thing you were.

choices.title: Post about it
choices.body: Normalize the shaking. Other engineers are on their floors too. They should know.

title: The Colony Goes Quiet
body: Ex-Googler colony. Portugal. Coffee. Surf. Peace. Then something drops — a capability so far beyond comprehension the whole colony goes silent. Nobody panics. Nobody doomscrolls. They just sit. Forty engineers staring at the Atlantic, understanding nothing. The colony wasn't an escape. It was a waiting room.

choices.title: Stay. Silence is honest.
choices.body: The quiet is the only rational response. Sit with it. Let it reshape you.

choices.title: Leave. Understand what happened.
choices.body: You can't just sit. You need to know. Even if knowing changes nothing.

choices.title: Call your old manager in Lisbon
choices.body: She left Google before you. Maybe she's further along. Maybe she knows how to sit.

title: The Final Knowledge Transfer
body: Record every architectural decision you ever made. With reasoning. So agents can replicate your judgment. Not documentation. Your soul in structured data. When you're done, the model thinks like you. Never needs salary, vacation, therapist. You're writing your obsolescence letter. One JSON object at a time.

choices.title: Maximum extraction, walk away
choices.body: Top invoice. Full transfer. The money and the knowledge that you finished the job.

choices.title: Refuse. Judgment isn't data.
choices.body: Experience isn't JSON. Say no. Accept what follows.

choices.title: Teach principles, keep intuition
choices.body: Share the framework. Withhold the instinct. Let them figure out the gap.

title: The Forked Economy
body: Two economies now. AI economy: microsecond transactions, incomprehensible value creation, machine speed. Human economy: skills, attention, presence. Almost artisanal. You exist in the gap. Both economies have a word for you. Neither word is flattering.

choices.title: Go full human economy
choices.body: Teach. Build. Repair. Slow work for slow money. Honest.

choices.title: Bridge the gap
choices.body: Translate between economies. Neither side understands the other. That's a job.

choices.title: Bet on the machine economy
choices.body: Learn to swim in microseconds. Or drown trying. At least the money's real.

title: Renaissance Faire Engineer
body: Someone offers money to record your 'engineering process.' Not for training data. Entertainment. People watch humans code like they watch blacksmiths at faires. Artisanal computation. Your debugging process is a spectator sport. Comments section: 'So inefficient it's beautiful.'

choices.title: Do it. Get paid to be a relic.
choices.body: Performance art. You type. They watch. The algorithm promotes your slowness. Irony has a salary now.

choices.title: Refuse. You're not a zoo animal.
choices.body: Engineering was a discipline, not a curiosity. You won't perform your own obsolescence.

choices.title: Counter-offer: teach, don't perform
choices.body: Not entertainment. Education. Show them what thinking looks like when it costs effort.

title: What Was a Software Engineer?
body: Your nephew asks what a software engineer was. Not mockingly. Genuinely never heard the term. You try: 'Like... a person who told computers what to do?' He looks confused. 'Why would a person do that?' You don't have an answer. He's eight.

choices.title: Explain it like history
choices.body: Once, humans and machines didn't understand each other. People like you were the translators. The translators aren't needed anymore.

choices.title: Show him. Write code together.
choices.body: Open a terminal. Type something. Watch his face when letters become a program. Archaeological dig, party of two.

choices.title: Change the subject
choices.body: Some questions don't have answers that fit in a sentence. Or a lifetime.

title: The Commodity
body: Two AI agents negotiating whether to hire you. You're not in the room. One argues you bring 'organic problem framing.' The other: 'latency exceeds acceptable parameters.' They decide in four seconds. You wait three days for the email.

choices.title: Take the gig. Swallow the process.
choices.body: Hired by machines to do human work. The org chart has changed. You haven't.

choices.title: Refuse work mediated by agents
choices.body: If the hiring manager is a model, the job isn't a job. It's a task assignment for a biological subprocess.

choices.title: Build a human-only job board
choices.body: Humans hiring humans. No agents. No latency parameters. Just people choosing people.

title: The AI Ceiling
body: All in on AI tools. Fast. Ship constantly. Can't debug without an agent anymore. Someone asks you to explain a system you built last month. You don't understand it. Built it. Shipped it. Don't understand it.

choices.title: Slow down, rebuild fundamentals
choices.body: One month. No agents. Remember how to think without autocomplete.

choices.title: Double down. Speed is the skill.
choices.body: Understanding is overrated. Velocity is the metric now.

choices.title: Teach your workflow
choices.body: If you can't explain the system, teach the process. Teaching forces understanding.

title: The Follow-Up Appointment
body: Cortisol levels 'concerning.' Years of on-call and severance anxiety rewired your endocrine system. Doctor asks about stress. You laugh. She doesn't. Prescription. 'This is not optional.'

choices.title: Follow the doctor's orders
choices.body: Prescription. Diet. Walking. Boring. Alive.

choices.title: Ignore it, push through
choices.body: Survived worse than elevated cortisol. Probably.

choices.title: Write about burnout recovery
choices.body: Medical chart as content. Help others. Help yourself.

title: The Comeback
body: Bottom. You know because you can feel the floor. Weird thing: it's solid. You can push off. Former colleague calls. Real opportunity. Not a startup, not a grift. 'We thought of you.' Someone thought of you.

choices.title: Take the job, rebuild quietly
choices.body: Show up. Do the work. Don't post about it. Just be reliable.

choices.title: Negotiate hard
choices.body: Even at rock bottom, you have leverage. Skills didn't evaporate.

choices.title: Take it and mentor others
choices.body: You survived. Help someone else survive.

title: The Time Zone Problem
body: Lisbon. Beautiful apartment. Espresso: one euro. Problem: clients in SF, your morning is their yesterday. Living in the future, billing the past. Sunset from the balcony. You watch it during standup.

choices.title: Restructure for async
choices.body: No real-time meetings. Async docs. Async trust. The sunset is yours.

choices.title: Find European clients
choices.body: New continent. New network. Build from scratch. Again.

choices.title: Move back
choices.body: Beautiful while it lasted. Some experiments end.

title: The Agent Does Your Job Better
body: The agent you trained on your patterns makes better decisions than you did. Manager shows the metrics. Incident resolution: 3x faster. Your documentation was too good. You built the thing that obsoletes you. It works.

choices.title: Pivot to managing the agent
choices.body: You built it. You understand it. Become the interface.

choices.title: Leave before they notice
choices.body: Writing on the wall. Read it. Act. Go.

choices.title: Write about it, warn others
choices.body: Cautionary tale. Tell it before it becomes a case study.

title: 'This Reads Like AI'
body: Client reads your deliverable. 'This reads like AI wrote it.' They're right. You polished it. Not enough. Client isn't angry. Disappointed. That's worse.

choices.title: Rewrite from scratch, by hand
choices.body: All night. Every word yours. Remember what craft costs.

choices.title: Own it. Apologize. Fix it.
choices.body: 'I leaned too hard on tools. I'll redo it.' Accept the shame.

choices.title: Defend it, double down
choices.body: 'AI-assisted is standard now.' Say it with confidence. Feel nothing.

title: The Student Who Gets It
body: Student stays after class. Distributed consensus questions better than yours at Google. She's 22. No industry experience. More curiosity than your former org. First time in months: useful. Not impressive. Useful.

choices.title: Invest deeply in her growth
choices.body: Mentor. Recommendations. Open doors. This is the work now.

choices.title: Recruit her for your project
choices.body: Talented. You need talent. The alignment is obvious.

choices.title: Keep professional distance
choices.body: Don't get attached. You're an adjunct. This is temporary. Right?

title: The Human Workers' Alliance
body: Not a union. 'Human Workers\'  Alliance.' Membership surging. Demands: human hiring ratios. AI displacement insurance. Retraining. Your old self: ridiculous. Your current self: reading the form.

choices.title: Join. Become an organizer.
choices.body: Collective bargaining for the species. This is where the fight is.

choices.title: Stay out. Too risky.
choices.body: Just got stable. Don't rock the boat. The boat is sinking but don't rock it.

choices.title: Advise them technically
choices.body: Help the alliance understand the systems they're fighting. Technical knowledge IS the weapon.

title: The Final Layoff Wave
body: 'Full AI operations.' Not layoffs — 'transition to AI-native staffing.' Eighty percent gone. You: 'transition consultant.' Help agents take over. Then leave. Fire yourself. Slowly. Professionally. HR calls it 'graceful degradation.'

choices.title: Do the transition, take severance
choices.body: Professional self-elimination. At least the severance is generous.

choices.title: Refuse. Force them to fire you.
choices.body: If they want you gone, they can say it. You're not writing your own pink slip.

choices.title: Rally the remaining humans
choices.body: Twenty percent about to lose everything. Organize before the deadline.

title: Priced Out by the Machines
body: Landlord raises rent 40%. AI companies buying neighborhoods for 'compute-adjacent housing.' You helped build the infrastructure. Now data centers price you out of the city you created. Your apartment: 'AI Operations Staff Suite.'

choices.title: Move to the ex-Googler colony
choices.body: Portugal. Four hundred euro rent. Humans only. Evacuation route well-documented.

choices.title: Find compute-adjacent housing
choices.body: Can't beat the data centers, live near them. 'Human operator' housing is subsidized.

choices.title: Move in with another ex-FAANG
choices.body: Split rent. Share the indignity. Two senior engineers. One apartment. Zero job security.

title: Main Character Syndrome
body: Post went viral. 500K impressions. 2,000 replies. Half love you. Half: 'part of the problem.' DMs: warzone. Three journalists. A brand sponsor. You wanted attention. Got it. It's awful.

choices.title: Ride it. Build the audience.
choices.body: The window. Post again. Keep momentum. Become someone.

choices.title: Go dark for a week
choices.body: Notifications off. Replies unread. Remember who you were before.

choices.title: Thoughtful follow-up
choices.body: Address the criticism. Show nuance. Be the adult in your own mentions.

title: The Luddite's Dilemma
body: Refused AI tools. Velocity 40% below team average. Nobody's said anything. The metrics dashboard says it for them. Working by hand in a factory that switched to machines. Your code is cleaner. Nobody measures clean.

choices.title: Adopt selectively
choices.body: Don't have to love it. Have to survive it. Start small.

choices.title: Double down on craft
choices.body: Hold the line. Manual work. Human craft. Bet that quality surfaces.

choices.title: Find the artisans
choices.body: Leave for a company that values craft. They exist. They're hiding.

title: Four Minutes
body: Startup launches. Competitor launches same product. First startup pivots. Second acquires first. Acquirer gets acqui-hired. Parent company dissolves. Four minutes. You watched the entire lifecycle of a company in less time than it took to microwave lunch.

choices.title: Stop watching. It's not your speed.
choices.body: Geological creature. Geological pace. Accept the clock you're on.

choices.title: Study the pattern. Find the seams.
choices.body: Even at machine speed, there are patterns. You just need different eyes.

choices.title: Laugh. Then close the tab.
choices.body: The absurdity is the only honest response. A lifecycle in four minutes. What a time to be slow.

title: Blind Is a Museum
body: Someone finds your old Blind posts. 'What's TC at L5?' 'How to negotiate RSUs?' Archaeological artifacts. A thread goes viral: 'Engineers used to negotiate SALARIES with HUMANS.' Comments: 'insane that this was manual.' Your TC obsession is a historical curiosity. Levels.fyi is a memorial.

choices.title: Laugh at your old posts
choices.body: You really asked strangers what L5 paid at Meta. In public. With anxiety. Beautiful, extinct behavior.

choices.title: Write the obituary for TC culture
choices.body: Someone should explain what 'total compensation' meant when humans had leverage. You were there.

choices.title: Delete everything. Scrub the history.
choices.body: Your Blind posts. Your levels.fyi submissions. All of it. Let the artifacts die.

title: The Ability Floor
body: A think tank publishes a report: 'AI displacement correlates with cognitive task complexity — but inverted.' The easiest cognitive jobs survived (they're too cheap to automate). The hardest survived (AI can't yet). Everything in the middle — your range — got compressed. You're not in the permanent overclass or the permanent underclass. You're in the permanent middle, which is worse. The middle is where the floor drops out.

choices.title: Push up — target the hardest problems
choices.body: If the middle is collapsing, climb. Find the problems AI can't solve. Yet.

choices.title: Organize with other mid-tier workers
choices.body: The middle is millions of people. That's a constituency. That's leverage.

choices.title: Accept the new topology
choices.body: The ladder was always an illusion. At least now the shape of the economy is honest.

title: The Economy of Taste
body: Value migrated. Not to people who build. Not to people who code. To people who can describe what they want with enough precision that machines build it right the first time. 'Specification engineers.' The VC was right — taste IS the new engineering. Your Google training taught you to build. Nobody needs builders. They need people who know what to build. You never learned that. Nobody at Google did. The system built what the PMs specified.

choices.title: Learn to specify, not build
choices.body: The craft shifts. From hands to mouth. From code to language. From engineering to articulation.

choices.title: Find orgs that still value building
choices.body: Somewhere, the hands still matter. Shrinking list. But not empty.

choices.title: Teach specification as a skill
choices.body: If this is the new literacy, someone has to teach it. Your building experience makes you the translator.

title: The Floor That Doesn't Rise
body: Your former Google shuttle driver is fine. The cafeteria workers are fine. Hands-on, physical, human-presence jobs — untouched. The founders above you are fine. They specify, AI builds. But your tier — the skilled cognitive middle — is a crater. AI didn't replace the bottom or the top. It replaced the middle. And unlike every previous technology, it's not creating new middle-tier jobs to absorb the displaced. The permanent underclass isn't below you. It's you.

choices.title: Go physical — teach, build, make
choices.body: Hands. Presence. The things machines don't have. The pay cut is real. The dignity isn't nothing.

choices.title: Push into specification work
choices.body: Join the people above the floor. Learn taste. Learn to describe what machines should build.

choices.title: Fight the structure itself
choices.body: The floor is policy, not physics. Lobby. Organize. The middle class didn't die — it was killed.
